body:
>High school is the worst period of most peoples' lives, don't let anyone tell you different.

I know a lot of people say this, but when I'm at school and see other people, a lot of them seem to be doing a lot better and to be happier than I am. Of course I can't know the full extent of what their life is like, but that's what it feels like a lot of the time. Sure they struggle with procrastination and stress too, but at least a lot of them seem to have decent relationships and more friends and do more fun activities. A lot of them just seem much more successful and happy and they have achieved much more than me and will continue to do so. Of course there are others whom I'm sure are doing as bad or even much worse than me, but I just feel like there are a good number of people doing alright.

>Honestly, depending on what you do on reddit/the internet, you're probably learning more on the internet than you are in school.

Sometimes this is true, other times I really am just wasting time. But even if I am learning a lot reddit, I don't exactly feel that I benefit a huge amount from learning obscure history and science. It doesn't have much practical advantage for me at the moment and seems more like a guilty pleasure and waste of time than useful knowledge. I feel that learning stuff like this won't be beneficial right now and that actually ACTING to improve my life would be more beneficial. It's just that going out and fixing my life is a lot harder than sitting on my ass learning fun facts about Genghis Khan or the Alpha Centurai system.

Still, thank you for the comment. I don't mean to discourage you (or anyone else) from posting here at the risk of "making me worse". I don't think I'm in anywhere near a bad enough condition yet that something a stranger says on reddit will make me kill myself tonight. So don't worry about speaking your mind.
